newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE white sugar lower but more tightness awaited.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE white sugar lower but more tightness awaited.

text.p: White sugar futures got off to a slow start on Wednesday morning with light spread trading and some flat-price selling after August's recent push through resistance, traders said.
At 1135 GMT volume was a light 266 lots, all in the two front months. August/October was trading at between $10.20 and $10.50, lower than earlier this week.
August stood 90 cents lower at $317.50 and October was down 50 cents at $307.00.
August broke through resistance at $317.50 on Tuesday to score a session high of $318.50 but has since eased back as players take profits.

But traders said it could still have room to the upside and possibly challenge $323.00, an area of highs dating back to last October as seasonal tightness is expected to boost the nearby price before expiry.
Traditional concerns about being short of the August position at the tail-end of European availability and ahead of the new crop were also supporting the market.
In physical news, Bangladesh is to issue two tenders later this month to buy a total 50,000 tonnes of whites but the exact dates and required shipment periods are as yet unknown.
In Paris only the nearby August contract traded, in a volume of just 105 lots. The position was 10 cents lower at $317.50.
